implementation_notes: unittest.mock is the stdlib realization: MagicMock creates callable attributes on demand, return_value/side_effect programme answers including exceptions and iterables, patch()/patch.object replaces the attribute in the namespace where the SUT looks it up and restores it afterwards, and assert_called_once_with/assert_called_with verify the interaction; create_autospec/autospec additionally makes the double fail on signature mismatches like the real object. The library follows the action-then-assertion model rather than record/replay, and a hand-written double is only necessary when the collaborator must be a genuine instance or when patching would reach too deep into the SUT.
code_sketch:
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

warehouse = MagicMock()
warehouse.has_inventory.return_value = True

order = Order("Talisker", 50)
assert order.fill(warehouse) is True

warehouse.remove.assert_called_once_with("Talisker", 50)
pitfalls: patch() must target the namespace where the SUT looks the name up, not the module that defines it; patching the definition module changes nothing observable.
A bare Mock accepts any attribute access and any signature, so a typo in an expected method name silently creates a child mock - use spec/spec_set or autospec to pin the interface.
Patching a coroutine with a plain MagicMock produces a non-awaitable double; use AsyncMock so await semantics are preserved.
